items.question: Codex on Windows sets no workspace env var; what is the one fixed project-source for Codex under D4?
items.recommendation: Use MCP roots/list first; if Codex never answers it, fall back to a single per-server resolve-once value set at spawn time, never a cwd/mtime heuristic. Add a GP7 contract test.

items.question: Is DeepSeek Harness (DSH) a v2.0 adapter, given D14 treats new adapters as separate scope and the issue gives no hook API detail?
items.recommendation: Defer DSH out of v2.0; no hook spec exists to build or test against. Revisit once DSH publishes a hook contract.

items.archaeology: 939c5ca8 (#103, 2026-03-13) 'fix: add process lifecycle guard to prevent orphaned MCP servers' — ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Detect parent death via ppid comparison, stdin close, and OS signals... Also adds WAL checkpoint on DB close to prevent SQLite lock contention.' INTRODUCED_BY: 939c5ca8. REGRESSION_RISK: per-tool-call CPU cost (55-70ms) was accepted as the price of a synchronous PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook; a v2 async PostToolUse must not lose the lock-contention protection that WAL-checkpoint-on-close gave. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep PreToolUse hook spawn under budget via a bundled TS hook (no DB open in the hook itself); PostToolUse may be async/fire-and-forget as long as it still appends to the journal exactly once.
items.question: What CPU budget applies to PreToolUse (sync, blocks the tool call) vs PostToolUse (can be async)?
items.recommendation: Fix the budget: PreToolUse <15ms CPU (bundled TS, no I/O, no DB open); PostToolUse async append-only, no budget beyond 'detached'. Encode both in GS6/GP3 contract tests.

items.question: D10 says hints only, no enforcement — does 'hint parity' across Pi and Claude Code (P2) require identical hint text, or just equivalent routing guidance?
items.recommendation: Require byte-identical hint text per tool across adapters (not just equivalent meaning), asserted by a GP-style contract test comparing Pi and Claude Code hint output for the same >50KB Read.

items.archaeology: 5e652e52 'feat(util/db-lock): per-DB lockfile primitive for single-writer enforcement' then 54ec1be7 'fix(util): delete db-lock.ts — single-writer primitive obsolete (v1.0.130 slice 4)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (5e652e52): enforce one writer per content DB because concurrent writers corrupted the store. It was later deleted once SessionDB became WAL multi-writer-safe (11e39301 ADR note). REGRESSION_RISK: if v2's content-store retention sweep (cleanupStaleSources) runs age-based deletion while a second session is mid-write, the same corruption class the lockfile existed to prevent can resurface. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: retention sweep must check liveness (PID), not just age, same as D6 session cleanup; never delete rows a live writer can still touch.
items.question: What is the retention rule for the content store (fetched/indexed sources): age-only, content-hash dedup, or liveness-gated like D6 session cleanup?
items.recommendation: Apply the same rule as D6: age threshold AND liveness check (no live PID holding that source open), never age alone. This closes the corruption path the old db-lock.ts was built to prevent.

items.question: D9/D11 drop the big snapshot/block but still inject 1-2 lines on SessionStart. On OpenCode (single-system templates) and Pi (cache-stable prefix), how are those lines carried without adding a new system message or busting the prompt cache?
items.recommendation: Merge the 1-2 lines into the adapter's existing single system entry (no new message), and persist them once per session so request N+1 has the same prefix as request N. Needs a GP2-style byte-stable-prefix test per adapter.

items.question: Same as #1085 — Pi's ephemeral tail injection breaks cache; what carrier keeps the prefix stable across a multi-request turn?
items.recommendation: Same fix as #1085: inject once, persist, never append ephemerally. Cover with GP2.

items.archaeology: 939c5ca8 (#103) introduced the parent-liveness/orphan-guard pattern (ppid + stdin close) that D6's 'live-PID safe' rule descends from. ORIGINAL_INTENT: never delete a resource a live process still owns. v1's cleanupOldSessions used WAL mtime as a liveness proxy, which issue #1140/#1024 show is wrong (idle-but-open sessions get evicted). REGRESSION_RISK: reintroducing any mtime-based heuristic in v2 repeats the exact bug #103 and #1024 were filed against.
items.question: D6 fixes PID-liveness + 14-day age for session DBs — is that the full rule, or does a size cap also apply?
items.recommendation: PID liveness check (never delete a DB with a live owning PID) AND age >=14 days from close time, no WAL-mtime heuristic. No size cap needed for session DBs specifically — size cap is a separate open question for the content store/journal (#961, #878).

items.question: With D10 removing hard denies, does a hint still reach the model when Claude Code fires several tool calls in one parallel batch (hint for call 1 can be buried by call 2's result)?
items.recommendation: Accept the loss for same-turn parallel siblings; add a PostToolUse/next-turn hint as backup when a WebFetch-class tool fired without the pre-hint being visible in the transcript. Needs a contract test asserting the backup path fires at most once per session.

items.archaeology: 939c5ca8 lineage not directly relevant; deny path for WebFetch is a D10 policy choice, not a historical fix being re-broken.
items.recommendation: D10 removes all hard denies, including the WebFetch deny that broke claude.ai artifact URLs. No decision needed beyond D10 itself; dup of #984/#938, same resolution.

items.archaeology: eb4f2a8c 'feat(setup): add --uninstall flag for clean removal' — v1 already has an uninstall flag. ORIGINAL_INTENT: give users a clean removal path after the self-heal/postinstall scripts (now removed under D2) left artifacts behind. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 drops `ctx uninstall` entirely, the exact 'leftover artifacts' complaint that drove eb4f2a8c returns, this time for MCP config + hooks.json instead of heal scripts.
items.question: Is `ctx uninstall` in v2.0 scope, and does it stop a running server before removing files?
items.recommendation: Keep uninstall in v2.0 scope (precedent exists in eb4f2a8c): remove every artifact install wrote AND signal the running server to exit (stdin close) before deleting its files. Same test as #1058.

items.question: What is Copilot CLI / Codex's one fixed project-source under D4 when no MCP roots are available?
items.recommendation: Resolve once per adapter from its own install/launch dir convention (e.g. Copilot CLI invocation cwd at spawn), with doctor erroring loudly if that resolution fails rather than silently falling back. Add GP7 rows per adapter.

items.question: D11 moves all routing prose into tool descriptions; #1031 shows that already costs ~6.2K tokens per call on Pi. What is the byte/token budget?
items.recommendation: Set a hard cap (e.g. <2K tokens total across all tool descriptions) and test it per adapter; this is C1 in map-I2 and must be resolved before D11 ships, since an unbounded description defeats the point of removing the routing block.

D4 'one fixed source via MCP roots, never process cwd' directly fixes the VS Code Remote-WSL case; r2's needs-decision tag was about the general D4-for-Codex ambiguity (#1210/#1017), not this VS Code row specifically. Add the GP7 VS Code row to confirm, but no open question remains for this issue.

items.question: Does honouring HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY for ctx_fetch_and_index need an SSRF check on the resolved proxy target, or can it just pass the env through?
items.recommendation: Honour the proxy env vars but validate the target host before CONNECT (basic SSRF guard: reject loopback/link-local/metadata-IP targets unless explicitly allow-listed). This is user-configured infra, not an LLM call, so D15 does not forbid it.

items.question: Should ctx_execute drop the code-echo-first-line behaviour by default, and add an optional `summary` arg?
items.recommendation: Drop code echo by default (first line must be a plain output summary per the map-I2 B requirement); add an optional `summary` arg for callers that want the command text repeated. Fixes #1047 and #1067 together.

items.question: Plan mode (Claude Code 2.1.228+) blocks ctx_batch_execute entirely — add a read-only gather tool, or accept the host's own plan-mode prompt?
items.recommendation: Add a read-only variant (search/read files only, no shell exec) that plan mode allows, rather than asking users to leave plan mode. This is the smaller, more honest fix than annotating ctx_batch_execute as read-only when it is not.

items.archaeology: Re-pointed per r2 note to ADR-0008 #6 + GP3.
items.recommendation: D10 (no hard denies) + D8 (hooks don't probe server state) removes isMCPReady and its OpenCode-embedded-mode redirect-swallow bug entirely. No open question; cite ADR-0008 #6 + GP3 test.

items.archaeology: Re-pointed per r2 note to ADR-0008 #4 + LV7.
items.recommendation: Same fix as #1053: isMCPReady and its deny path disappear under D10/P2. No open question; cite ADR-0008 #4 + LV7 test.

items.archaeology: eb4f2a8c 'feat(setup): add --uninstall flag for clean removal' (precedent for cleanup scope); 2f457d2a 'fix(setup,adapters): resolve second-pass workflow findings' shows uninstall correctness was revisited more than once in v1 — it is a recurring regression class, not a one-off.
items.question: Does uninstall remove the cache dir and stop the live MCP server, or only settings/hooks entries?
items.recommendation: Full removal: settings/hooks entries, cache dir, and signal the live server to exit (same as #1016). A single `ctx uninstall` command, verified by diffing install-then-uninstall state to empty.

items.question: Should every ctx_index `--source` label include the path, or stay a bare label, given D12 ranks hits by labelled source?
items.recommendation: Make the label always path-qualified (e.g. `docs/foo.md` not `foo`) so D12's source-count and ranking logic has a stable, collision-free key.

items.archaeology: ab5aad90 (2026-03-06) 'fix: soft-fail shell exit code 1 when stdout has content' — ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Shell commands like grep exit 1 for no matches — not a real error.' classifyNonZeroExit() was built specifically so a timeout/kill does NOT get the soft-fail treatment. REGRESSION_RISK: a v2 hard kill-on-timeout must still route through the same non-zero-exit classifier, or killed commands will be misreported as a soft grep-style non-error. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: timeout/cancel must set a distinct exit signal (SIGKILL/process-group kill) that classifyNonZeroExit (or its v2 equivalent) always treats as a real error, never soft-fail.
items.question: What is the default server-side timeout value, and does kill-on-timeout target the whole process group (Windows: Job Object)?
items.recommendation: Kill the whole process tree (process group on POSIX, Job Object on Windows) on timeout or client cancel, within 2s; exit code from a kill must never be classified as grep-style soft-fail. Fix once, reuse for #936, #947, #959.

items.question: Does v2 read host permission profiles (Codex settings, CC permissions) at all, or only its own config?
items.recommendation: Read only context-mode's own config; do not parse host permission/security files. D10 already removes hard denies, so there is nothing for a host permission profile to gate — reading it would be dead code.

items.question: Does the batch timeout bound the whole handler (exec + index + search), not just the child process?
items.recommendation: Timeout wraps the full handler; indexing/search after exec must be cancellable too, same kill-tree mechanism as #936.

D6 (14-day age + live-PID safety) covers session DBs; legacy v1 sessions/ dir is separately flagged by doctor per D13. No open question for this row; r2's needs-decision tag applies to the general retention question (#1079/#1156), already answered there.

items.question: Same timeout/kill-tree question as #936, specific to Pi's abort signal.
items.recommendation: Honour the host abort signal by killing the same process tree as the timeout path; event loop must never block waiting on the child. One mechanism for timeout, cancel, and abort-signal.

items.question: What are the numeric total-byte and chunk budgets for indexing batch output, and what happens above the limit?
items.recommendation: Fix explicit numbers (not implied by truncation, per the no-truncation-as-reduction owner rule): index up to max_total_indexed_bytes, and report in the reply that output was cut rather than silently dropping bytes. Needs the number chosen and a unit test, not just a policy sentence.

items.question: How is trigram/vocabulary growth bounded for logs/JSONL content — porter-stemming only above a size threshold, high-entropy token filtering, or both?
items.recommendation: Apply a high-entropy token filter (drop tokens that look like hashes/UUIDs/base64) plus porter-only indexing above a size threshold; needs the threshold number fixed before it is testable.

findings.claim: 71 rows are tagged needs-decision with no owner answer recorded; several (e.g. #1056/#988 multi-writer DB, #1121 soft-fail exit code) have a v1 fix already on record that answers the underlying question but r2 does not cite it.
findings.evidence: git log shows 939c5ca8 (#103, WAL checkpoint on close) and ab5aad90 (classifyNonZeroExit) as the original fixes behind the #1056/#988 and #1121 questions; neither commit is referenced in ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2 for those rows.
findings.archaeology: 939c5ca8 'fix: add process lifecycle guard... Also adds WAL checkpoint on DB close to prevent SQLite lock contention'; ab5aad90 'fix: soft-fail shell exit code 1 when stdout has content'.
findings.fix: Cite these commits directly in the ADR/decision text for #1056 (DB checkpoint ownership) and #1121 (kill exit codes must never be classified soft-fail), per the recommendations above.

findings.claim: C1 (#1031 tool-description token budget) is flagged as an open contradiction but has no numeric cap proposed anywhere in the reviewed docs.
findings.evidence: map-I2.md line 63: 'D11 needs a size cap' with no number given; ADR-0011 not read for a cap (out of the ADR set named in this task).
findings.fix: Set an explicit token budget for all tool descriptions combined (recommend <2K tokens) and add it to ADR-0011 or TECH-SPEC.
